title: Brugada Criteria for VT vs SVT with Aberrancy
keywords: absence of RS in precordial leads
purpose: A four-step sequential rule to distinguish ventricular tachycardia from SVT with aberrant conduction in a regular wide-complex tachycardia. Work through the steps in order — a 'yes' at ANY step means VT and you stop. Only if all four are 'no' is SVT with aberrancy favoured.

items.label: Step 1 — Absence of an RS complex in ALL precordial leads (V1–V6)?

options.label: No — an RS is present somewhere

items.label: Step 2 — In any precordial lead with an RS, is the R-to-S-nadir interval > 100 ms?
Step 3 — Is there AV dissociation (more QRS than P, capture or fusion beats)?

Step 4 — Morphology criteria for VT present in BOTH V1–V2 and V6? (RBBB pattern: V1 monophasic R / qR / broad R; V6 R:S < 1 or QS. LBBB pattern: V1–V2 broad R > 30 ms, slurred/notched S downstroke, > 60 ms to S nadir; V6 any Q wave)

interpretation.label: All four steps negative — SVT with aberrant conduction is favoured. Still treat cautiously; if there is ANY doubt or haemodynamic compromise, manage as VT. Adenosine may be used diagnostically/therapeutically only if the rhythm is regular and monomorphic and VT is thought unlikely

One or more steps positive — VENTRICULAR TACHYCARDIA. If unstable: synchronised cardioversion. If stable: amiodarone (or procainamide, which is first-line in the guidelines for stable monomorphic VT) and prepare for cardioversion. Do NOT give AV-nodal blockers (verapamil, diltiazem, adenosine bolus as 'treatment') — they can precipitate collapse

notes: Default assumption in any wide-complex tachycardia, especially with age > 35 or known structural heart disease / prior MI, is VT — the Brugada algorithm's specificity for SVT is imperfect (later studies show lower accuracy than the original 1991 paper). Other clues favouring VT: QRS > 160 ms, extreme axis (−90° to ±180°), precordial concordance, a QRS in aVR starting with a tall R (Vereckei aVR criterion), history of CAD/CHF.
buildNote: Sequential rule — any positive step → VT; the point sum is a helper, not a graded risk.
